limitations: Integrity is an exact-envelope SHA-256 checksum with checked projections; it is not a signature, independent anchor, or protection against a privileged administrator rewriting both envelope and digest.

The owner must supply already-authorized server-derived identity, action/result meaning, policy/approval evidence, data classification and applicable retention-class references. Their presence does not itself authorize an operation.
Staging is not durable success; the authorized owner must commit its configured transaction.
Owner-specific production retention/holds, audit search permissions, key/anchor policy and legal/production acceptance remain with their approved capabilities.
Required role reviews are Codex engineering reviews, not independent human or legal acceptance.
acceptance_results: Immutable event fields and defensive reference snapshots implement Document 28 section 9 without arbitrary object payloads.
Operation/correlation and applicable causation/evidence/approval/version references are preserved exactly.
Pristine records verify; single-byte envelope corruption and divergent indexed projection fail integrity checks.
Real PostgreSQL round-trip preserves exact envelope bytes and full original time; timestamp projection uses explicit microsecond precision.
Database guards reject UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE; duplicate and concurrent same-ID writes cannot replace the original.
Existing transactional-outbox boundary commits owner/audit/outbox together and rolls back flushed audit/owner writes after failure or cancellation.
No Product workflow, audit UI/search, retention duration, legal policy, provider transport, public API or new authority record was introduced.
